claims.text: The high-temperature stability of disordered BCC Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is governed by competition between configurational entropy and negative Al–X mixing or ordering enthalpies.
The Al–Cr, Al–Fe, Al–Co, and Al–Ni interactions have negative mixing enthalpies.
When T·ΔS_conf exceeds the magnitude of the Al–X ordering enthalpy, the BCC lattice remains chemically disordered.
When T·ΔS_conf falls below the Al–X ordering enthalpy magnitude, Al-driven B2-type ordering occurs.
Quenching Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 from 1100 K produces a homogeneous, single-phase, disordered BCC initial state.
The controlled intervention is 2 h isothermal annealing at temperatures from 600 to 1000 K followed by rapid quenching.
The comparison holds composition, specimen form, atmosphere, annealing time, and heating/cooling rate fixed while varying annealing temperature.
The relevant structural mediator is the degree of Al–X short-range chemical ordering within the BCC lattice.
Superlattice peak intensity can measure the degree of Al–X chemical ordering.
Configurational entropy stabilizes disordered BCC at high temperature, whereas the enthalpic drive for Al–X ordering promotes B2-type order upon cooling.
Annealing at or above 950 K will yield no B2 superlattice reflections, with the specified peak intensity below 1% of the fundamental.
Annealing at or below 850 K will yield B2 superlattice peak intensity above 10%.
Samples annealed at or below 850 K will exhibit a DSC exotherm associated with ordering.
A sharp ordering transition occurs between 850 and 950 K.
The as-homogenized sample quenched from 1100 K has superlattice peak intensity below 1%.
The as-homogenized sample quenched from 1100 K has a flat DSC baseline.
The proposed validity is limited to bulk Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7, annealing times up to 2 h, and heating/cooling rates of at least 100 K/min.
The predicted ordering threshold has an uncertainty of ±50 K because of kinetic barriers and measurement precision.
Detection of B2 superlattice peaks after annealing above 950 K would falsify the stated prediction.
Absence of ordering signatures after annealing below 850 K would falsify the stated prediction.
